<p dir="auto">I view GDPR the same way I view VAT, which we do not fully support in core.</p>
<p dir="auto">If we add full support for GDPR then we should likewise add full support for VAT and other country / region specific laws (thinking of Germany here). When do we determine when and when not to support non-global regulations?</p>
<p dir="auto">I suppose my main hesitation in adding GDPR specific features is "when does it stop?" conundrum?</p>
<p dir="auto">At this time I'd like to propose that compliance features be built through a free add-on that we (EDD) put on an "officially approved" recommendation list. data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><p dir="auto">Right now I'd say we need to see what 'tools' the core team makes available to Plugin developers. There is a lot of talk around a couple solutions:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>Creating a way to register certain data as private</li>
<li>A Request log, for site owners to work through.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">I think one of the important things that EDD will have to monitor is compliance with other eCommerce data laws like VATMOS which requires keeping customer data for a timeframe, however, if that user requests to have their data anonymized/removed, what implications does that have for the store owner to remain compliant from an accounting/tax perspective?</p>
<p dir="auto">Sounds like the Core team has some ideas moving forward on how to build out some of these 'audit' tools, and if possible I'd prefer that we simply hook into those, instead of building a whole new UI for it.</p>
<p dir="auto">I'd for one think that we need to keep transactional data in place. If a user decides to request their data be scrubbed, I feel like we need to keep the payment record mostly in tact however some of the data is important for tax reporting for the business owner (like the billing address) , we could simply scrub the customer data to be anonymous, while still unique.</p>
<p dir="auto"><a href="https://make.wordpress.org/core/2018/02/19/proposed-roadmap-tools-for-gdpr-compliance/" rel="nofollow">https://make.wordpress.org/core/2018/02/19/proposed-roadmap-tools-for-gdpr-compliance/</a></p></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1
